<description>
This PR catches two birds with one stone:

- fixes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36515
- adds a `Block` interface, which lets IPC clients fetch the block data (or its header)

This means a client can still fetch (and store) the block after `submitSolution()`, but we no longer mutate the template's `CBlock` for this.

### Block interface

`submitSolution()` no longer modifies the template. It applies the solution to a copy of the template block and returns a `Block` handle for that copy, also when the block is rejected.

`Mining::submitBlock()` and `BlockTemplate::block()` do the same. The new interface has a `data()`, `header()` and `coinbaseMerklePath()` method, so these are migrated from the `BlockTemplate` interface.

The interface can be expanded later, e.g. to tell whether the block is part of the active chain (or went stale, useful for a miner to know).

This is a breaking change for IPC clients:

- `getBlockHeader()` → `block().header()`
- `getBlock()` → `block().data()`
- `getCoinbaseMerklePath()` → `block().coinbaseMerklePath()`
- `bool submitSolution(..., reason, debug)` → `Block submitSolution(..., accepted, reason, debug)`
- `bool submitBlock(block, reason, debug)` → `Block submitBlock(block, accepted, reason, debug)`

It uses new ordinals and old methods throw.

`submitSolution()` now throws when the coinbase is null, instead of returning false.

### Performance

My agent measured how long after `submitSolution()` sv2-tp forwards the next template, with master as the baseline and an adapted sv2-tp as the client:

| Workload | Master | This PR | Paired median difference (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty block | 1.32 ms | 1.40 ms | +0.05 ms [−0.11, +0.15] |
| Near-full block, 3.7 MB | 10.11 ms | 10.07 ms | −0.09 ms [−0.44, +0.28] |

The extra `block()` call costs about 0.15 ms per template for a C++ client. The alternative approach of having `submitSolution()` return the full `CBlock` added 6ms.
</description>

[2026-11-19] r:5968390827 review COMMENTED by xyzconstant (contributor):
Code review 1f9fcfab45fa2bdd8296c265dfac2dd206a353bc

The approach is sound to me, but now the `Block` capability served to clients holds references to TXs that might leave the mempool. IPC clients now take responsibility for dropping these block capabilities and as a result freeing up memory on the node (good this is that this is trivial to inspect with the `getMemoryLoad` method proposed in #33922). This behaviour change should be documented in the PR description and the first commit msg.

Planning to review more.
